verdict.rationale: LiteLLM Proxy documents its own MCP Gateway, which gives agents one fixed endpoint for all MCP tools with access control by key and team. Admins can register MCP servers in the UI, and tools are also exposed via REST list/call endpoints. However, the evidence shows only an aggregating proxy for third-party MCP servers. It does not show an official LiteLLM MCP server exposing LiteLLM's own capabilities as tools, and nothing confirms agent connections work in practice. missing for 10: official MCP tools for LiteLLM's own functions (spend, keys, models), documented agent/client connection setup and transports, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can connect an agent via an official MCP server

citations.quote: LiteLLM Proxy provides an MCP Gateway that allows you to use a fixed endpoint for all MCP tools and control MCP access by Key, Team.
On the LiteLLM UI, Navigate to "MCP Servers" and click "Add New MCP Server".
